positive.description: Settings for a new study vault
positive.prompt: Set up the Obsidian settings for a new study vault for my statistics course.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_vault_config with vault_type studies and returns the .obsidian files (app.json, appearance.json, core-plugins.json, page-preview.json, graph.json, snippets/callouts.css, snippets/concept-cards.css) and the folder list Lectures, Labs, Concepts, Formulas, Examples.

positive.prompt: I want a work vault for my team's project notes, written in Polish. Which Obsidian settings and folders should it have?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_vault_config with vault_type work and spellcheck_language pl; app.json lists pl as the spellcheck language and the folders are Projects, Meetings, Companies, People, Decisions, Concepts.

positive.prompt: Show me the vaultcraft template for a concept note.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_note_template with kind concept and shows the template, which starts with frontmatter (tags, source, status, difficulty) and a definition callout.

positive.description: Broken link with a suggested fix
positive.prompt:
Check these vault notes for broken links:
Concepts/TF-IDF.md: '---
tags: [concept]
source: "[[L01 - Intro]]"
---
> [!definition] TF-IDF
> Weights a word by how rare it is.

Builds on [[Bag of Word]].'
Concepts/Bag of Words.md: 'Counts words. See [[TF-IDF]].'
Lectures/L01 - Intro.md: 'First lecture.'
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_vault with the three notes and reports 5 issues: the broken link [[Bag of Word]] in Concepts/TF-IDF.md with the suggestion [[Bag of Words]]; Bag of Words has no incoming links; TF-IDF has no example and fewer than 2 outgoing links; L01 - Intro does not list TF-IDF.

positive.description: Build a vault from lecture notes
positive.prompt: Build an Obsidian study vault from these lecture notes. Use the defaults.
positive.expected_behavior: The vaultcraft skill asks its intake questions or accepts the defaults, writes concept and lecture notes from the attached files, calls check_vault on them, fixes reported problems, and returns the vault as a zip file to open in Obsidian.
